2027 Toyota Crown Signia Gets GT-S Concept Treatment for SEMA, Becomes a Sleek Wagon
25 photos
Photo: Toyota
The 2026 SEMA Show is just around the corner, and automakers are slowly unveiling the vehicles they created specifically for this event. Toyota has already revealed a lineup of five SUVs and trucks with snow tracks , but it will also put a sportier rig on display. Meet the Crown Signia GT-S Concept.
Unveiled for the 2025 model year in North America, the Crown Signia is a mid-size crossover. It's not the bulkiest SUV out there, but it's not exactly sporty-looking either. Well, the GT-S Concept fixes that, turning the Signia into a sleek station wagon.
Built by the Toyota Motorsports Garage, the GT-S Concept looks like its ready to hit the Nürburgring for a few fast laps. For starters, it rides nearly five inches (127 mm) lower than the stock model thanks to a set of custom, one-off MCS (Motion Control Suspension) coilovers.
But the lowered suspension isn't the only feature responsible for the vehicle's car-like appearance. It also rides on motorsport-like 21-inch HRE wheels wrapped in Toyo tires , both of which are tucked under widebody fenders.
Up front, the GT-S Performance Concept flexes a massive grille that puts the Crown Signia almost into Lexus territory. The black side inserts have also grown larger, while the upper thin grille and the badge have red accents (because red makes everything look sportier, right?).
The rear fascia received similar attention, with every single letter finished in red. But the main highlight here is the black diffuser with six vertical fins, flanked by trapezoidal exhaust tips. That's one aggressive-looking rear end! The aero package is rounded off by a pair of vents carved into the upper front fenders.
The slammed crossover is also finished in a custom-mixed dark gray metallic paint with added flake and several coats of clear for extra sheen. It's not the flashiest paint job out there (though it may look better in person), but it certainly fits the motorsport-inspired theme.
Toyota didn't have much to say about the interior, but the images reveal heavily bolstered front seats with red accents and "GT-S" lettering on the headrests. The gear lever also has a red insert for an extra dash of color in an otherwise very black interior.
Toyota had nothing to say about the vehicle's drivetrain but mentioned that stopping power comes from calipers sourced from the Lexus RX 500h F Sport. Needless to say, the GT-S Concept is probably stock otherwise, meaning that it utilizes the same 2.5-liter inline-four engine as the regular Crown Signia.
The mill is paired with two electric motors and delivers a total of 243 horsepower through an eCVT transmission. Toyota offers both hybrid and plug-in hybrid versions , by the way.
Does this concept preview a production model? Well, I wouldn't get my hopes up. The company states that it was put together with "parts and accessories not available from Toyota" and stresses that the modifications "may negatively impact vehicle performance and safety and may not be street legal."
But needless to say, I wouldn't mind seeing a beefed-up version of the Signia in showrooms at some point.
